The statement is cautiously supportive: the Fed eases 25 bps and stabilizes funding markets (T-bill purchases and repos) to sustain expansion amid below-target inflation and global uncertainties. In New Keynesian evidence where expectations anchor inflation dynamics (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) and flexible inflation targeting aims to keep expectations from drifting (Svensson), persistently low market-based inflation compensation justifies accommodation. The noted weakness in business fixed investment is macro-salient because investment is highly cyclical and sensitive to internal finance and liquidity conditions (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994), so easing can help offset capex headwinds. VAR-based studies (Sims; Zha) and policy surveys (McCallum and Nelson, 1999) document that rate cuts can support real activity, while smooth money-market operations aid transmission. Netting strong labor and consumption against soft capex/exports and sub-2% inflation, the tone skews modestly positive but risk-aware rather than outright upbeat.

“This action supports the Committee’s view that sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee’s symmetric 2 percent objective are the most likely outcomes, but uncertainties about this outlook remain.”
